key: Let him not love to speak ill words: but fear the One who holds all four Within his hand, until they fall.
s: A hymn on those the Adityas guard ends with a warning about speech; Sāyaṇa, on 1.41.9, takes the four as cowrie shells in a game of dice, their holder feared by the other player until they fall, as evil speech should be feared.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.41.9, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 350337 (2022)

opened.edition: Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921)

evidence.words: "दुरुक्ताय "न "स्पृहयेत् दुष्टं वाक्यं न कामयेत् किंतु दुरुक्तात् "बिभीयात् । तत्रावशिष्टो मन्त्रभागः सर्वोऽपि दृष्टान्तः । चित् इत्युपमार्थे वर्तते । अक्षद्यूतं कुर्वतोरुभयोर्मध्ये यः पुमान् "चतुरः चतुःसंख्याकान् कपर्दकान् "ददमानात् ददतो हस्ते धारयतः पुरुषात् "आ "निधातोः कपर्दकनिपातपर्यन्तं बिभीयात् अस्य जयो भविष्यति न भविष्यति इत्यन्यो भीतिं प्राप्नुयात् । अत्र यथा भयं तथा दुरुक्ताद्भेतव्यमिति धर्मरहस्यम् ।
evidence.gloss: One should not desire evil speech (durukta) but should fear it. The rest of the verse is all a comparison; cit carries the sense of a simile. Between two playing at dice, one fears the man who holds four cowrie shells in his hand, until the shells fall: whether he will win or not, the other is seized by fear. As fear is here, so evil speech should be feared: this is a secret of dharma.

reason: Second judgement, the refutation upheld as a correction. Re-opened packet.js veda 5 --verse 1.41.9: the evidence is verbatim and the cowrie reading (कपर्दकान्) is Sāyaṇa’s own; Wilson’s note confirms it (Sayana says, four cowri shells) and Yāska, Nirukta 3.16, has dice. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.41.9, at [40,9]); the hymn’s last verse, so the plain sense (a hymn on those Varuna, Mitra and Aryaman protect, closing on speech) is faithful and repeats no four words of the key. Changed: the earlier sentence made the shells ‘dreaded by the other player’, but Sāyaṇa makes the man holding them the one feared (ददतो हस्ते धारयतः पुरुषात् … बिभीयात्), the other fearing whether he will win; the reading now says their holder is feared until they fall, as evil speech should be feared (यथा भयं तथा दुरुक्ताद्भेतव्यम्). Same key, ref, src and evidence.
